author: andyundso
body:
This PR switches the pipeline for tiny_tds from CircleCI to GitHub Actions.

Functionality-wise, they should be equivalent, although I made a couple of additions:

- The ports are compiled in one step for all the Linux jobs, similar to how we do this for Windows.
- Test summary is displayed for each job, e.g. [here](https://github.com/andyundso/tiny_tds/actions/runs/8806805186). 
- The built gem versions for Windows can also be downloaded from that page.
- I also test the installation of the gem on Mac with M1 processors. This was something I added once to CircleCI for #545, only to realise it is only available for paid organizations.

Open questions / points from my side:

- Currently, the installation on Windows for MSSQL 2017 is broken, so I commented it out in the matrix and reported an issue upstream (https://github.com/potatoqualitee/mssqlsuite/issues/27). Worst case we could re-activate the solution we used for CircleCI, as I did not find another action that can install multiple versions of SQL server and on different platforms. I could also fork (or re-implemented) a similar solution on my own time.
- `docker-composee.yml` currently uses the CircleCI Ruby image. I like having this compose file around for a quick start into tiny tds development, but I would suggest to switch the official Ruby images from Docker Hub.
- There are a bunch of scripts we no longer would need (like `setup_cimgruby_dev`).

author: bdteo
body:
This pull request addresses an issue where the PHP version was incorrectly determined on macOS within the configure_package function. The root cause was that macOS's native grep command lacks support for the -P option.
To resolve this, the following changes have been made:

Implemented a polyfill for macOS's version of grep to ensure compatibility. The polyfill modifies the grep arguments by replacing -P with -E when necessary.
Enhanced the debug output by adding more detailed information during the debugging process. The added debug output provides valuable insights into variables and their values, facilitating easier troubleshooting.
Updated the .gitignore file to exclude JetBrains IDE and Mac OS X system files, keeping the repository clean and focused on relevant files.

These changes improve the reliability and usability of the php-build tool on macOS systems. The polyfill ensures that the PHP version is correctly determined, while the enhanced debug output aids in identifying and resolving issues more efficiently.
Please review and consider merging these changes to enhance the compatibility and debugging capabilities of php-build on macOS.

Best Regards,
@bdteo

author: robinmalfait
body:
This PR introduces a new `portal` prop, and fine-tunes the meaning of the `modal` prop on the following components:

### `Combobox` component

The `ComboboxOptions` component now accepts two new props:

- `portal` (boolean, defaults to `false`): Whether to render the options in a portal. This will always be set to `true` if an `anchor` prop is passed.
- `modal` (boolean, defaults to `true`):
  - Enables scroll locking, which means you can't scroll the page
  - Enables `inert` on other elements, which means you can't interact with other elements on the page while the combobox is open. An outside click typically requires two clicks. The first click will close the combobox, and the second click will interact with the element.

### `Listbox` component

The `ListboxOptions` component now accepts two new props:

- `portal` (boolean, defaults to `false`): Whether to render the options in a portal. This will always be set to `true` if an `anchor` prop is passed.
- `modal` (boolean, defaults to `true`):
  - Enables scroll locking, which means you can't scroll the page
  - Enables `inert` on other elements, which means you can't interact with other elements on the page while the listbox is open. An outside click typically requires two clicks. The first click will close the listbox, and the second click will interact with the element.

### `Menu` component

The `MenuItems` component now accepts two new props:

- `portal` (boolean, defaults to `false`): Whether to render the options in a portal. This will always be set to `true` if an `anchor` prop is passed.
- `modal` (boolean, defaults to `true`):
  - Enables scroll locking, which means you can't scroll the page
  - Does not enable `inert` on other elements, which means you can interact with other elements on the page while the menu is open. This also allows you to tab to the next focusable element.

### `Popover` component

The `PopoverPanel` component now accepts two new props:

- `portal` (boolean, defaults to `false`): Whether to render the options in a portal. This will always be set to `true` if an `anchor` prop is passed.
- `modal` (boolean, defaults to `false`):
  - Enables scroll locking, which means you can't scroll the page
  - Does not enable `inert` on other elements, which means you can interact with other elements on the page while the menu is open. This also allows you to tab to the next focusable element.

body:
### Which issue this PR addresses:

[ARO-6773](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ARO-6773)

Fixes

### What this PR does / why we need it:

**I will be closing this PR once [PR #3741](https://github.com/Azure/ARO-RP/pull/3741) is merged**.

This is needed for a resilent to failure RP deployment.
Our current implementation has shown some faults over time with RP deployments, and need improvements in general.  

[Custom scripts Tips](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/extensions/custom-script-linux#tips) Recommends scheduling a reboot if it is needed. This is to allow all other VM extensions to complete their setup. If the VM is rebooted while they are executing setup steps, they will fail to finish.
Therefore, I have made all system services start at the end of the script, made firewall rules effective in runtime, and scheduled a reboot 1 hour after the script finishes. 

Move all shared code into a commonly shared file to be sourced by all
bootstrapping scripts. This allows for code reuse, minimal duplication.

### Test plan for issue:

Tested bootstrapping scripts in an Azure VM using image RedHat:RHEL:8-lvm-gen2:latest.  
Mainly to catch missed syntax errors, and ensure files written are formatted as expected.  

Fully tested with deployment to INT and FF INT. [Successful Deployment and E2E](https://msazure.visualstudio.com/AzureRedHatOpenShift/_build/results?buildId=95439277&view=results)

[Second INT test run](https://msazure.visualstudio.com/AzureRedHatOpenShift/_build/results?buildId=97407813&view=results)

If you would like to test these bootstrapping scripts out yourself, here are some helper functions.

```bash
# testing_vm.env

export RESOURCEGROUP="${USER}-bootstrap-test"
export VM_NAME="$RESOURCEGROUP"
```

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# manage_testing_vm.sh

vm_create() {
    check_vars

    # os disk size is set to 256GB to allow testing of configure_disk_partitions
    az vm create --nic-delete-option Delete --public-ip-address pubIP --public-ip-address-allocation dynamic -g $RESOURCEGROUP -n $VM_NAME --image RedHat:RHEL:8-lvm-gen2:latest --ssh-key-values ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub --public-ip-address-allocation static --os-disk-size-gb 256
}

vm_delete() {
    check_vars

    az vm delete -g $RESOURCEGROUP -n $VM_NAME -y
}

check_vars() {
    echo "RESOURCEGROUP=${RESOURCEGROUP:?Please export RESOURCEGROUP}"
    echo "VM_NAME=${VM_NAME:?Please excport VM_NAME}"
}
```

Here is a helper environment file, to avoid failures for unset env variables.  

```bash
# rp_boostrap_testing_variables.env
# rpVMSS.sh
export RPMDSDCONFIGVERSION=empty RPMDSDNAMESPACE=empty MDSDCERTIFICATESAN=empty LOCATION=eastus RPMDSDACCOUNT=empty MDSDENVIRONMENT=empty PORTALELEVATEDGROUPIDS=empty DATABASEACCOUNTNAME=empty KEYVAULTPREFIX=empty RPMDMACCOUNT=empty RPPARENTDOMAINNAME=empty RPIMAGE=empty AZURECLOUDNAME=empty MDMIMAGE=empty FLUENTBITIMAGE=empty LOGKIND=empty MDMFRONTENDURL=empty MDMSOURCEENVIRONMENT=empty MDMSOURCEROLE=empty MDMSOURCEROLEINSTANCE=empty KEYVAULTDNSSUFFIX=empty ACRRESOURCEID=empty ADMINAPICLIENTCERTCOMMONNAME=empty ARMAPICLIENTCERTCOMMONNAME=empty ARMCLIENTID=empty FPCLIENTID=empty FPSERVICEPRINCIPALID=empty BILLINGE2ESTORAGEACCOUNTID=empty CLUSTERMDMACCOUNT=empty CLUSTERMDSDACCOUNT=empty CLUSTERMDSDCONFIGVERSION=empty CLUSTERMDSDNAMESPACE=empty CLUSTERPARENTDOMAINNAME=empty GATEWAYDOMAINS=empty GATEWAYRESOURCEGROUPNAME=empty RPFEATURES=empty CLUSTERSINSTALLVIAHIVE=empty CLUSTERDEFAULTINSTALLERPULLSPEC=empty CLUSTERSADOPTBYHIVE=empty USECHECKACCESS=empty DBTOKENCLIENTID=empty GATEWAYSERVICEPRINCIPALID=empty PORTALACCESSGROUPIDS=empty PORTALCLIENTID=empty

base64_empty="ZW1wdHkK"
export ADMINAPICABUNDLE="$base64_empty"
export ARMAPICABUNDLE="$base64_empty"

# devProxyVMSS.sh
export PROXYIMAGE=empty PROXYIMAGEAUTH=empty AZURECLOUDNAME=empty
export PROXYCERT="$base64_empty"
export PROXYKEY="$base64_empty"
export PROXYCLIENTCERT="$base64_empty"

# gatewayVMSS.sh
export DBTOKENURL=empty GATEWAYFEATURES=empty GATEWAYMDSDCONFIGVERSION=empty AZURESECPACKVSATENANTID=empty AZURESECPACKQUALYSURL=empty
```

Simply `scp` the files you would like to test to your newly created VM, and execute them.  

```bash
. testing_vm.env

vm_create
RESOURCEGROUP=steven-bootstrap-test
VM_NAME=steven-bootstrap-test

bootstrapper_vm_ip="Replace with VM IP address output from above"

scp pkg/deploy/generator/scripts/devProxyVMSS.sh "$bootstrapper_vm_ip":
scp pkg/deploy/generator/scripts/commonVMSS.sh "$bootstrapper_vm_ip":
scp pkg/deploy/generator/scripts/gatewayVMSS.sh"$bootstrapper_vm_ip":
scp pkg/deploy/generator/scripts/rpVMSS.sh "$bootstrapper_vm_ip":
scp ~/Documents/bootstrap_vmss_testing/rp_boostrap_testing_variables.env "$bootstrapper_vm_ip":
```

When you're done testing, delete the vm.

```bash
vm_delete
RESOURCEGROUP=steven-bootstrap-test
VM_NAME=steven-bootstrap-test
```

author: aleksandrsim
body:
This pull request introduces support for ONNX runtime in the `predictor.py` and `decoder.py` modules, allowing users to leverage optimized ONNX models for faster inference compared to the original PyTorch models. This is particularly beneficial for deployment in resource-constrained environments where inference speed is crucial.


### Changes:
1. **Initialization of ONNX Runtime Session:**
   - Added a new function to initialize an ONNX runtime session with support for multiple providers (TensorRT, GPU, CPU) in priority order. This allows users to maximize the performance based on their available hardware.

2. **Modification to `predictor.py`:**
   - Extended the `predictor.py` to accept an ONNX model checkpoint path.
   - The predictor now can operate in two modes: using the original PyTorch model or the ONNX model depending on the user’s choice.
   - It extracts necessary metadata from the original model checkpoint which is still required for complete functionality.

3. **Update to `decoder.py`:**
   - Adjusted `decoder.py` to handle the decoding operations based on whether the ONNX model is being used.
   - Ensured that the input image size matches the ONNX model’s required input shape to avoid errors during inference.


I am looking forward to your feedback and suggestions on this new feature addition. Please let me know if there are any other aspects or tests you would like me to consider. Thank you for reviewing this enhancement for better inference performance with ONNX support.

author: ericbandrews
body:
Changes the way `ActiveAccount` is initialized:
- Guest mode and user mode now have two separate initializers
- The guest mode initializer just takes the `URL` of the instance rather than an `ApiClient`

This approach makes the behavior of the initializer more transparent, removes the possibility of initializing a user account with an `ApiClient` pointing to a different instance, and removes the need to spin up `ApiClient`s just to call the guest mode initializer.
